items.text: Munoz completed a permanent GBP22m move from Crystal Palace to Nottingham Forest, a three-year deal and a direct request from Oliver Glasner, who managed him before. He was a regular starter and a key contributor at Palace, so his 0.36 availability on your board is the same new-club discount hitting Marmoush, not a form or fitness concern - treat him as a starter, not a bench risk.

Reversing the bench read published last night: multiple reports now have Garner set to start for Everton against Manchester United on Sunday, with Hackney a doubt after picking up a knock. Sky Sports says Garner is playing well enough to be linked with an England call-up.

Leeds boss Daniel Farke confirmed centre-back rival Joe Rodon has a hamstring injury and will be out for eight to ten weeks, removing Bijol's main competition for a starting spot for the rest of this international window and beyond.

Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi said Marmoush is available to play, possibly from kickoff, against Forest - direct manager confirmation for a player who only just arrived on loan from Man City alongside Savio. The model's availability figure has been rising with the news but is still a step behind what the manager is actually saying.

Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage confirmed at today's press conference that Jean-Philippe Mateta is injured with a hamstring problem and out for three weeks, telling reporters "Mateta is injured, now for three weeks." That removes Strand Larsen's only rival for the striker spot, and he leads the line again at Fulham on Saturday - the model's 0.74 availability figure undersells how secure his role now is.

Brentford captain Nathan Collins was forced off after just 17 minutes of today's 1-1 draw with Sunderland with a calf strain. Boss Keith Andrews said "It's a calf strain, I don't know the extent" - your model still rates him a nailed starter at 1.00 availability, so this is one to watch rather than act on yet.

Bijol was left out of Leeds' starting XI against Brighton today - Nico Elvedi and Tarik Muharemovic started in central defence instead - and only came on as a 61st-minute substitute. That is his first confirmed bench appearance of the season and the model's 0.92 availability figure has not caught up with it.

Igor Jesus was not even named among Nottingham Forest's substitutes for today's goalless draw with Tottenham - Liam Delap started up front and it was Chris Wood, not Jesus, who came on at striker. The model still rates Jesus a 0.95-availability, near-top free agent forward; that number is now stale.

Reversing Tuesday's read: Palace's own matchday report confirms Eddie Nketiah, not Strand Larsen, led the line at Fulham on Saturday, with Strand Larsen only introduced at half-time. Palace's own preview had flagged the change beforehand, calling it Sage's decision with Strand Larsen 'on the bench for this one' - the model's 0.69 availability figure still reads him as the clear first-choice striker, which is no longer true with Nketiah, Mateta and Strand Larsen genuinely rotating.

Reversing Saturday night's report that Garner played the full 90: Everton's own lineup data shows he was substituted in the 77th minute of Sunday's 2-2 draw with Man Utd for Ainsley Maitland-Niles, having gone down in visible pain. The club now lists him with an unspecified injury and only a 75% chance of playing next time out - the model's own board already flags him as a drop candidate on the back of it.

Free agent Tyrick Mitchell scored twice as Crystal Palace came from behind twice to beat Fulham 3-2 for their first league win of the season - a nailed-on starter delivering well above his defensive price point, and a stronger claim target than Justin's own Munoz, who remains an impact substitute at Forest.

Doku's calf return is now being pointed toward the Manchester derby on 13 September, per the Premier League's own injury tracker - a date that falls after GW4's own waiver deadline (12 September), not just after the GW4 waivers window. He remains unavailable for the entire GW4 window regardless of which reading of his return is correct.

Correction to Saturday's item: Sky's own team sheet for Forest v Spurs lists Igor Jesus among the substitutes and shows him coming on in the 59th minute, alongside Daniel Munoz - he was not left out of the squad, and Chris Wood came on separately at 74. The real change is that he has lost his starting place: he started GW1 and GW2 and Liam Delap led the line on Saturday. The model still rates him the best free-agent forward available at 11.8 over the next five.

Barcola finally got his first Liverpool start tonight, in the Champions League against Atletico Madrid, then went down clutching his calf in the 58th minute and had to be replaced - ESPN's live commentary called it a spell that 'doesn't look great' for him. After three weeks of single-cameo minutes, this is a fresh fitness question rather than the pure selection one this week's claim was built on, and it pushes his path into the Premier League XI further away, not closer.

Ben Chilwell has re-signed for Crystal Palace and scored the winner at Fulham with his first touch, having come on for Tyrick Mitchell on 73 minutes. Mitchell scored both of Palace's other goals and is the pick of the free-agent defenders this week, but Chilwell plays his position and is now in the building - one to watch rather than a reason to pass.

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola confirmed Barcola's exit at the hour mark against Atletico Madrid was cramp, not an injury, saying he is 'very happy' with the forward's first start and two clear second-half chances on goal. That corrects last night's 'doesn't look great' read, though it changes nothing about the underlying case: Barcola still has zero Premier League minutes started this season and faces Gakpo, Isak and Ngumoha for a place at Fulham on Saturday.

Iraola told Friday's press conference that Barcola's cramp is not an injury and he 'should be available' for Saturday's Fulham game if training goes to plan - a likely second Liverpool start. The model still has him at just 0.16 availability and 2.4 next5, the same blind spot every marquee mid-season arrival runs into: it cannot see a player easing into a new team, only a name with no minutes.

Tottenham's own site confirms James Maddison is back in Roberto De Zerbi's plans and Mohammed Kudus - who can play 'as a winger, as a number 10, as a striker up front' - is 'very close to being ready to start', while Mykhailo Mudryk has been ruled out six to eight weeks with an ankle injury from his Forest debut. One rival for Marmoush's central role has gone, but two more are converging on the same weekend.

Free agent Jannik Schuster made his Premier League debut replacing the injured Nathan Collins on Saturday, and Brentford's own site quotes Keith Andrews saying part of the decision to let Ethan Pinnock leave was confidence in Schuster's ability - he 'was thrown into it today and he produced.' The model has him at just 0.31 availability off a single appearance, the same blind spot that undersells every new arrival.

Strand Larsen scored twice in Tuesday's Carabao Cup win over Middlesbrough, per Crystal Palace's own match report, strengthening his case to lead the line at home to Ipswich today with Mateta still out - a firmer position than last week's bench role behind Nketiah, though no permitted outlet has published today's confirmed XI yet.

Confirmed: Strand Larsen leads the line again for Palace against Ipswich this afternoon, with Tyrick Mitchell at wing-back - Crystal Palace's own team news has Nketiah failing his pre-match fitness test after 'we knew he was a doubt', resolving this morning's open question in Strand Larsen's favour.

Barcola starts for Liverpool against Fulham this afternoon, his second start in four days after Tuesday's Champions League appearance against Atletico - Liverpool's own site confirms it, with Iraola turning to him again on the left. The model still has him buried at avail 0.26 and next5 3.5 off zero career games in its sample, well behind what two straight starts for a fit forward should be worth.

Newcastle's deadline-day arrival Matias Fernandez-Pardo, a reported 51m signing from Lille, is "getting closer to starting" according to boss Matthias Jaissle ahead of the Leeds trip, having so far only appeared from the bench against Bournemouth. The model still rates him bottom of the free-agent forward board at 0.19 availability and a 2.7-point next5 off zero Premier League games - the same blind spot that undersold Barcola for weeks.

Milenkovic and Cunha both started Forest's full 90 minutes in Saturday's 2-1 win at Aston Villa, Igor Jesus scoring an 88th-minute winner - this week's recurring hamstring doubt did not materialize. The model's 0.60 availability for Milenkovic looks conservative; the Hill-for-Milenkovic waiver claim now rests on fixture value alone, not fitness.

Correction to last night's report: ESPN's own live commentary shows Milenkovic and Cunha did not play Saturday's 2-1 win at Villa Park - both dropped out with hamstring tightness found in Friday's training, Diomande and Munoz starting in their place. Glasner expects Milenkovic to also miss the Coventry game, with a return targeted for the fixture after.

Bogle scored in Leeds' 4-1 demolition of Newcastle on Monday night, netting in the 34th minute as part of a 3-0 half-time lead, per Newcastle's own match centre. The model's next5 figure for him (12.6) is built on fixtures and form, not tonight's goal, so treat this as a point in his favour that the board hasn't priced in yet.

Newcastle's 51m deadline-day signing Matias Fernandez-Pardo got his full first-team debut in that same Leeds game, but Jaissle hooked him at the 57th minute with the score already 3-0, per the club's own match centre. The model still rates him bottom of the forward pool off essentially no minutes (avail 0.19, next5 2.7) - a real data point at last, though one bad afternoon does not settle whether he starts again against Bournemouth.

Mohammed Kudus made his first Tottenham start since January in Wednesday's Carabao Cup exit at Liverpool, but Marmoush also started and played the full 90 in a heavily rotated XI - the pecking order for Justin's forward has not shifted yet, though Kudus's return is a fresh name to watch.

Maresca left Haaland and Gvardiol out of Manchester City's squad entirely for tonight's Carabao Cup tie with Norwich - Man City's own site frames it as workload rotation after Sunday's derby, not injury, with both expected back for Sunday's league game at home to Sunderland. Worth knowing before a blank appearance tonight reads as a fitness concern on the board.

Adrien Truffert, this week's top waiver target for Justin's defence, has earned his first call-up to the senior France squad, per Bournemouth's own site - recognition for a player who started all 38 league games last season and is in career-best form now. It doesn't change the case for claiming him, just reinforces it.

Anton Stach, Justin's rank-3 GW6 waiver target, has been named in Jurgen Klopp's first Germany squad on the back of an eye-catching debut season at Leeds - a form signal for a player already on the claims board as the upgrade on Lewis-Potter, not a change to his role at the club.

Raya started as normal in goal for Arsenal's 3-0 defeat at Brighton today (Gross, Kostoulas, Chema Andres) - the loss is on the defense in front of him, not a fitness issue, and a clean team sheet finally retires the recurring 'knee bandaged' Raya injury story that has resurfaced and been discarded on four separate runs since 5 September.

Free agent Pascal Gross scored the opener in Brighton's 3-0 win over Arsenal today, with Kostoulas adding a second before half-time - live evidence for the model's own suggested Gross-for-Barcola swap (+15.1 next5), which this week's claims board again declined given Barcola's own two straight Liverpool starts.

Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage said this week he hopes Mateta and Dean Henderson will return only 'after the international break,' pushing his striker's timeline further out than earlier estimates and cementing Strand Larsen as Palace's clear starting forward through the whole GW6 waiver window.

Leeds' own team news for today's home game against Crystal Palace has Bogle among the substitutes, the first time all season a permitted source has actually left him out of the XI - James Justin comes in at right wing-back, with Joe Rodon and Jaka Bijol both restored to the back three. The model's 0.89 availability figure has not caught up with it yet.

Sunderland's deadline-day signing of Malick Fofana from Lyon, a deal worth up to GBP30m that owner Kyril Louis-Dreyfus personally flew to Lyon to close after Crystal Palace tried to hijack it, is the same blind spot that hit Barcola and Munoz: the model has him at just 0.15 availability and a 2.1 next5, near the bottom of the free-agent midfield pool. He has only started for Sunderland in the Carabao Cup so far and has yet to nail down a Premier League place.

runs.note: Morning sweep ~11 hours after last night's 21:11 run. Club-by-club pass on every squad club (Everton, Arsenal, Leeds, Brighton, Hull, Tottenham, Man City, Liverpool, Brentford, Bournemouth, Crystal Palace) plus today's live GW5 fixtures (Man City-Sunderland, Leeds-Palace, Bournemouth-Liverpool) and the free-agent shortlist clubs, about 20 searches. Led with a direct fetch of leedsunited.com's own team news for today's Palace game, which has Bogle among the substitutes for the first time all season - James Justin in at right wing-back, Rodon and Bijol restored to the back three - a genuine surprise the initial aggregator search had wrongly reported as an unchanged Leeds XI with Bogle still starting. Second item: Sunderland's deadline-day, up-to-GBP30m signing of Malick Fofana from Lyon (owner personally flew out to beat a Crystal Palace hijack) is the same new-arrival blind spot as Barcola and Munoz, and the model still has him at the bottom of the midfield pool. Chased down and discarded two stale stories masquerading as current: a 'Pickford out a month with a thigh injury' Sky Sports piece that dates to 2022-09-07, and the recurring Raya thigh-injury/Bolton-squad story that traces to the same 2024-09-27 arsenal.com article flagged stale on four earlier runs - both would have been real news if current, so worth the direct fetch-and-check each time they resurface. Also checked and found nothing further to publish: Tottenham's Van Hecke and Marmoush are both pencilled into the predicted XI for the Villa game with Van Hecke 'fresh after being rested at Anfield', Man City's Haaland (rested midweek, back to lead the line) and Gvardiol both set for today's Sunderland game, and Bournemouth's and Brentford's injury lists (Araujo, Kroupi, Adli, Milosavljevic; Dasilva, Milambo, Collins, van den Berg, Furo, Jensen) contain no squad or shortlist names. A Premier League transfer-news search also surfaced a 'Gross and Dunk to miss Sunday vs Bournemouth' line that contradicts Brighton's own site (Gross the club's standout performer, next match is Man Utd away in the cup, not Bournemouth) - discarded as a mismatched/stale result.

Morning sweep ~11 hours after last night's 21:11 run. Club-by-club pass on every squad club (Everton, Arsenal, Leeds, Brighton, Hull, Tottenham, Man City, Liverpool, Brentford, Bournemouth, Crystal Palace) plus two general PL sweeps, 15 searches. Led with Stach's Germany call-up (leedsunited.com). Chased down one lead in depth that did not survive: a widely-repeated 'Raya limping, bandaged knee, fears of a serious setback' story after a Man City game - this is the same stale item flagged and discarded on 18 September, traced back to a 27 September 2024 Etihad fixture (the Neto-debut game), not anything current; his four full 90s this season already contradict it, so left unpublished. Also checked and found nothing citable: Vuskovic (cramp only, fine per Brighton's own read), Gvardiol (a recurring stale 'broken leg' search result contradicted by his own recent minutes), Anderson (cramp substitution, no concern), and Truffert/Tavernier both fit and playing for Bournemouth. Reconfirmed unchanged: Pickford, Bogle, Ajayi, Van Hecke, Lewis-Potter, Scott, Tavernier, Schade, Marmoush, Strand Larsen and Haaland all training and selected normally with nothing citable that changes a status.

Morning sweep ~10.5 hours after last night's 21:09 run, and the last run before today's 17:30 UTC GW5 deadline. Club-by-club pass on every squad club (Everton, Arsenal, Leeds, Brighton, Hull, Tottenham, Man City, Liverpool, Brentford, Bournemouth, Crystal Palace) plus two general PL sweeps, 16 searches. Nothing survived that both moves a verdict and clears a permitted source. Chased down two leads in depth: Hull's Semi Ajayi has search results claiming he 'missed Hull's last six fixtures' since an AFCON hamstring injury and is only 'expected to rejoin full training next week' (Yahoo/hayters.com), but this contradicts multiple fresher predicted lineups for Saturday's Newcastle game that all have him nailed at centre-back, and the AFCON injury dates to January - treated the six-fixtures story as a stale aggregator mix-up rather than current, no permitted outlet carries it either way, so left unpublished and his status stands. Also checked whether Van Hecke's Carabao Cup bench role at Anfield signals anything - predicted lineups have him back in Tottenham's XI for Saturday's Villa game, but that is rotation for a cup tie, not news, and no permitted outlet has published tomorrow's confirmed XI yet. Reconfirmed unchanged: Raya, Bogle, Vuskovic, Gvardiol/Haaland (both still pencilled in for Sunday after last night's rest), Barcola, Lewis-Potter, Scott, Tavernier, Schade, Marmoush and Strand Larsen all training and selected normally with nothing citable that changes a status. Nothing published.

Second run today, ~1.5 hours after the 19:30 sweep that built the first GW6 claims board and the GW5 deep starters pass. Fresh club-by-club sweep on every squad club (Everton, Arsenal, Leeds, Brighton, Hull, Tottenham, Man City, Liverpool, Brentford, Bournemouth, Crystal Palace, Nottingham Forest) plus two general PL injury/lineup sweeps, about 19 searches. Nothing moved: Arsenal's own site still has Saliba out and Timber a late fitness test, neither a squad player of Justin's; Raya's only injury history is an old thigh knock already recovered from, no fresh concern; Crystal Palace's own coverage reconfirms Mateta out until after the international break with Strand Larsen leading the line, and Sarr/Nketiah also doubtful, all already priced in; Leeds have Gruev, Gudmundsson and Gnonto working back into training but nothing on Bogle; the Premier League's own injury tracker (updated today) lists Spurs absentees as Kudus, Maddison, Kulusevski, Odobert and Solanke - Marmoush and Van Hecke are not on it, reinforcing both as fit. Checked the GW6 free-agent targets (McBurnie, Stach, Anderson, Truffert, Timber) for anything that would change this morning's claims board - nothing new turned up. Nothing published.

Manual off-schedule run at Justin's request, ~11 hours after this morning's sweep, and the first run after GW5 waivers processed (deadline tomorrow 17:30 UTC) - also did the weekly deep starters.json pass this run. Club-by-club sweep on every squad club (Everton, Arsenal, Leeds, Brighton, Hull, Tottenham, Man City, Liverpool, Brentford, Bournemouth, Crystal Palace) plus free-agent-target clubs (Fulham, Nottingham Forest, Sunderland, Coventry) and two general PL sweeps, roughly 30 searches. Led with Man City resting Haaland and Gvardiol entirely for tonight's Carabao Cup tie with Norwich - mancity.com's own team news frames it as pure workload management after Sunday's derby, both pencilled back in for Sunday's Sunderland game, so a blank appearance tonight shouldn't read as a knock. Investigated and could not publish: a Sports Mole-only claim of a Raya knee injury after the Man City game never turned up on arsenal.com or Sky Sports, and Arsenal's own site is currently focused on Saliba (out) and Timber's return, not Raya, so left alone as unconfirmed; Ajayi's hamstring situation remains murky - Sky Sports' own lineup confirms he played and scored against Man Utd on 22 August, but no permitted outlet has since published his hamstring recovery timeline (only Yahoo and fan sites), so his status stays as already modelled rather than published as news either way. Confirmed but not new: Van Hecke, Marmoush, Bogle, Vuskovic, Strand Larsen, Tavernier and the rest of the squad all training and playing normally with nothing citable that changes a status. Full starters.json deep pass done this run - see its own run log for the gameweek-by-gameweek verdicts.

Second run today, ~13 hours after the 08:15 sweep. Full club-by-club pass (Everton, Forest, Brentford, Leeds, Man City, Liverpool, Bournemouth, Palace, Tottenham, Man Utd, Sunderland) plus general PL injury/transfer searches. Led with Barcola: he started tonight's Champions League tie with Atletico Madrid, his first start for the club, and went off in the 58th minute holding his calf (ESPN live commentary) - a genuine new fitness question, not just a minutes one. Also checked Leeds: BBC Radio Leeds pundit Adam Pope reportedly said Bijol's Brighton bench call was a reward for Elvedi's training form rather than injury-related, but that only reached a permitted outlet via Yahoo/aggregator reprints of the podcast, not bbc.co.uk itself, so it stays unpublished - does not change the Bijol drop either way. Doku confirmed still pointed at the 13 September derby (after GW4's deadline) with no fresher permitted-source date. Collins' calf still has no confirmed Brentford timeline - the only 'return date' found (RotoWire, 12 September) is an algorithmic estimate, not a club statement, and RotoWire is not a permitted source. Nketiah, Mitchell, Le Fee, Maguire, Hill, Scott and the rest of the squad and free-agent shortlist checked and unchanged from this morning.

First run of the day, ~11 hours after last night's 21:12 sweep. Full club-by-club pass on every squad and free-agent-target club (Everton, Arsenal, Forest, Brentford, Leeds, Man City, Liverpool, Bournemouth, Palace, Tottenham, Sunderland, Man Utd, Brighton) plus general PL injury/transfer and rival-player searches, roughly 30 queries in total. Nothing survived that both moves a verdict and clears a permitted source. Checked specifically: Maguire's new Man Utd contract (real, manutd.com, but signed back on 2 August - not fresh, and doesn't change his nailed status which is already priced in); Liam Delap's Forest transfer (completed 27 August, already reflected in Igor Jesus's drop from the XI reported last week); Doku, via premierleague.com's own O'Reilly/Doku update - Maresca says only 'we need to wait' on the derby and Doku was left out of the Champions League squad for Porto, restating rather than changing the existing read; Bijol/Elvedi at Leeds - no fresh Farke team news since last week's Brighton bench call. Two genuine fixtures kick off later tonight (Chelsea vs Leeds, Carabao Cup; Liverpool vs Atletico Madrid, Champions League) that could move Bijol and Barcola respectively, but neither has been played yet as of this run - worth a same-day follow-up once they finish. Nothing else moved on Collins, Munoz, Marmoush, Strand Larsen or the free-agent shortlist. Nothing published.

Full club-by-club sweep ~13 hours after this morning's run (Everton, Nottingham Forest, Brentford, Leeds, Man City, Liverpool, Bournemouth, Crystal Palace, Tottenham, Arsenal, Sunderland, Man Utd) plus general PL injury/transfer searches. One lead investigated in depth but not published: BBC Radio Leeds commentators reportedly noticed Bijol struggling in the warm-up before Saturday's Brighton game and in discussion with medical staff, but the only place carrying that is Yahoo Sports and Leeds aggregators reprinting the radio commentary - no bbc.co.uk or leedsunited.com page surfaced it, so it stays unpublished (he is already treated as benched regardless of the reason). Also checked whether Sage has said anything decisive on Strand Larsen vs Nketiah ahead of the Ipswich game - only unpermitted previews (Sports Mole, Yahoo, lastwordonsports) claim Nketiah is now sidelined and Strand Larsen the clear leader; cpfc.co.uk's own site did not surface a matching press-conference page, and search results for Leeds/Palace kept mixing in stale prior-season articles (an April hip-flexor reference for Bijol, a hamstring story for Nketiah from a different season), so nothing there cleared the bar either. Collins' calf still has no confirmed Brentford timeline beyond 'don't know the extent'. Doku still stuck on Maresca's 'we're not sure yet, we need to wait' for the derby, unchanged from Sunday. Munoz, Marmoush, Garner, Le Fee, Milenkovic, Gvardiol, Haaland, Tavernier and Raya all confirmed exactly as already priced in, with no fresh fixtures since the weekend's round. Nothing published.

Third run today, ~6.5 hours after the 14:49 update. Full club-by-club sweep (Everton, Man Utd, Forest, Man City, Leeds, Brentford, Liverpool, Bournemouth, Palace, Tottenham, Sunderland, Brighton) plus two general searches. Nothing material and new survived: Collins' calf still has no confirmed timeline from Brentford's own site; Bijol still Leeds' fourth centre-back per last week's Brighton team news, with nothing fresher published since; Munoz remains an impact sub rather than a confirmed starter for Forest, still working into full fitness after his mid-week move; Doku's own manager, Maresca, said today only 'Jeremy, we're not sure yet, we need to wait' on the Man Utd derby (13 September) - restates the existing doubt rather than changing it, since that match falls after GW4's own deadline regardless. Maguire took a bloody nose in the Everton draw but played on and shows no fitness concern. Checked Le Fee, Barcola, Strand Larsen, Groß, Kostoulas and Maguire himself - all unchanged from what's already published. Nothing published.
seeded by hand while building the pipeline
Garner's pre-season groin surgery - explains an availability number the model could only read as 'not playing'

Marmoush (Man City to Spurs, started and impressed on debut) and Munoz (Palace to Forest, permanent, Glasner's man) both hit the same new-club-discount blind spot the model has for Barcola - both are mine, both look like bench risks on the dashboard and are actually starters
Woltemade (mine, weakest forward) loaned out to Juventus on deadline day - he is out of the Premier League entirely, not just out of favour, which the 0.37 availability figure did not capture

Munoz correction (he's competing with Aina for the RB spot, not a guaranteed starter as reported yesterday), Garner benefiting from Hackney's ankle knock, and Palace's Mateta hamstring injury opening the door for free agents Strand Larsen and Nketiah

Leeds' Rodon (hamstring) and Gruev (meniscus) both sidelined, thinning the competition for Bijol's centre-back spot. Checked rivals' best assets (Bruno Fernandes, Mbeumo, Guehi, Dewsbury-Hall) for league-scope news but every lead traced back to stale Dec 2025/pre-season stories, not current - nothing else published this run

Ran club-by-club searches on every squad member and free-agent target (Munoz/Aina, Garner, Bijol's rivals, Woltemade, Palace strikers, Bournemouth and Brighton free agents) but every lead just re-confirmed what was already published earlier today - the one new item was a fresh (17:10 UTC) pundit piece projecting Marmoush inside Tottenham's actual strongest XI going forward, not just a one-off debut start, which the model's 0.35 availability still does not reflect

Munoz reversal - Forest's own predicted XI (published this morning) has him starting at right wing-back against Spurs, not competing with Aina as reported Tuesday, so he comes off the drop list this week; and Barcola is now confirmed live in the FPL pool with a possible bench debut Friday at Ipswich, still rated near the bottom of all free agents by the model. Full club-by-club refresh (Everton, Arsenal, Forest, City, Leeds, Brentford, Fulham, Bournemouth, Tottenham, Newcastle, Brighton) plus rivals' best assets (Bruno Fernandes, Palmer, Gibbs-White, Semenyo) found nothing else new or actionable

Full deep-research pass ahead of GW3's deadline (squad now final after waivers processed): corrected Tuesday's misread on Garner (he was a sub, not a starter, at Preston - he's behind Hackney for Sunday), found Doku's calf return has slipped to 13 September (GW4) not the 5 September date shown on the dashboard, and confirmed Igor Jesus as Forest's nailed-on striker ahead of Chris Wood in red-hot preseason form. Also ran a full club-by-club sweep across all 15 squad players for starters.json - see claims.json and starters.json for what changed there.

Re-run 13 minutes after the last deep pass ahead of GW3's deadline (17:30 UTC tomorrow). Ran a fresh sweep across every squad club (Everton, Forest, Man City, Leeds, Bournemouth, Brentford, Palace, Tottenham, Liverpool, Sunderland) plus rivals' best assets - Rodon's 8-10 week hamstring, Doku's calf, Munoz's Forest debut, Marmoush vs Solanke, and Barcola's expected bench debut are all confirmed exactly as already published this evening. One search flagged a possible Solanke ankle knock, but a follow-up read found only stale July/August articles referencing his prior surgery, not a current one, so nothing new to add or correct.

Full club-by-club sweep ~11 hours ahead of the GW3 deadline (17:30 UTC). Two corrections against last night's read: Garner is now set to start against Man Utd (Hackney a doubt with a knock), and Solanke's ankle injury (out since early August, major doubt) removes the competition threat to Marmoush that was cited last night, with Marmoush now in Tottenham's predicted XI. Also checked Brentford (two search hits on Schade/Collins injuries turned out to be stale articles from a prior season and were discarded), Leeds (Bijol still locked in alongside new signing Elvedi), Bournemouth (Hill, Rayan, Tavernier all in the predicted XI), Crystal Palace (Strand Larsen confirmed starting with Mateta out until October) and Liverpool (Barcola still expected on the bench for his debut at Ipswich tonight) - all unchanged from what's already published.
dropped 17 of 19 items whose only citation was off the SOURCES list

Two items the source purge had removed, republished with permitted citations found this run: Rodon's 8-10 week hamstring injury (clears Bijol's path at Leeds, leedsunited.com) and De Zerbi confirming Marmoush available, possibly from the start, against Forest (tottenhamhotspur.com). Also re-sourced starters.json and claims.json this run - see their own run logs. Nothing else material found in a fresh club-by-club sweep, including a check on Strand Larsen (his old 'leading the line' claim did not survive a fresh look at the source, which turned out to be nine months stale, so not republished).

Full club-by-club sweep ~8 hours after the last run (Everton, Arsenal, Forest, Man City, Leeds, Brentford, Liverpool, Bournemouth, Tottenham, Palace, Sunderland) plus two general searches on deadline-day fallout and rivals. Everything already published held up: Garner still favoured in Everton's predicted double pivot for Sunday even with Hackney now cleared of his ankle knock, Bijol has no fresh fitness concern ahead of Brighton, Strand Larsen is confirmed leading the Palace line at Fulham, and Doku's calf timeline still points past GW4's deadline. One lead - conflicting reports that Ola Aina, not Munoz, starts at right wing-back for Forest against Tottenham - never cleared a permitted outlet (only Sports Mole, GiveMeSport and thehardtackle carried it), so it was left out rather than reversing Wednesday's Forest-sourced correction on a weak citation.
